matches.rationale: These findings collectively identify that the paper's aberration/reference-frame treatment (invalid covariant velocity derivation in Eq.3, double application of SR transformation to the already-geometric FLRW aperture in Eqs.6/11-18, an invalid invariant phase-space claim underlying Eqs.19-20, and the resulting non-standard luminosity/angular distance definitions in Eqs.16/24/29/39/40) all stem from incorrectly mixing the galaxy's cosmological frame with a special-relativistic boosted frame relative to the observer — exactly the mechanism described in the ground truth. Findings 5 and 6 instead flag separate algebraic/sign inconsistencies in the H(z) and r1 equations that are not tied to the reference-frame conflation.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Identifies the invalid treatment of galaxy velocity via an illegitimate metric-lowering of coordinates, the root of the frame-mixing error.
Shows the aberration correction double-counts geometry already present in FLRW, directly reflecting the mistaken assumption of a distinct galaxy frame.
Continues the same thread, showing the resulting distance definitions are shifted by an extra (1+z) factor due to the same frame-mixing derivation.
Points out the invalid invariant phase-space claim used to justify the extra beaming/aberration factor, part of the same flawed frame treatment.
Flags a genuine sign/formula inconsistency in the H(z) expressions, unrelated to the reference-frame assumption described in the ground truth.
Identifies a separate algebraic inconsistency in the r1 equation and curvature limit, not connected to the frame-mixing defect.
